# Multi-Output Requirements Checklist: Summoned Dot-Field Volume OSD

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency and measurability of the focused-output, per-display edge, configuration-migration and multi-monitor acceptance requirements
**Created**: 2026-11-23
**Feature**: [Specification](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are placement requirements defined for every summon source: automatic audio changes, shell volume/mute actions, show-only actions and pointer-edge dwell? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-017–020]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements complete for selecting the focused-window display, the pointer display when no window is focused, the configured fallback and the final available-display fallback? [Completeness, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK003 Are placement-lock requirements defined for every visible phase—emerging, interactive and retracting—and for new audio changes received during those phases? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK004 Are independent left/right side selection, same-side copy, mirrored copy and the requested right/right profile all explicitly required without implying duplicate OSD instances? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, Clarifications 2026-11-23]
- [ ] CHK005 Are the exclusive ownership and intentional non-delivery of top- and bottom-edge surfaces both stated, so reserving those zones cannot silently expand this feature? [Scope, Spec §FR-017, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK006 Are requirements present for valid v1 migration, invalid migration input, unsupported versions and the prohibition on rewriting user configuration? [Gap, Plan §Technical Context, Configuration Contract §Schema-v1 migration]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Is “display containing the keyboard-focused window” defined clearly enough to distinguish it from compositor-focused workspace/output state? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK008 Is “pointer display when no window is focused” qualified by the Niri focus-follows-mouse prerequisite and by the behavior required when that prerequisite is absent? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020, Plan §Multi-output routing and edge zones]
- [ ] CHK009 Is “usable edge” consistently defined as the logical vertical output edge on the initial baseline, including the limitation around third-party reserved areas? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, Assumptions; Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the integer division rule for heights not divisible by three explicit about which zone receives the one- or two-pixel remainder? [Clarity, Data Model `EdgeZone.bounds`]
- [ ] CHK011 Are copy/mirror source identity, invalid references, cycles, disconnected outputs and fallback behavior described with one unambiguous meaning? [Clarity, Configuration Contract §Per-output trigger profiles]
- [ ] CHK012 Is “full dismissal” tied to a named lifecycle boundary so placement re-resolution cannot occur at different times in different requirements? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020, Data Model `Osd.phase`]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK013 Do the specification, configuration contract and data model agree that side selection is per output with a global right-side default? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Configuration Contract `edge.side`/`edge.outputs`, Data Model `EdgeTriggerProfile.side`]
- [ ] CHK014 Do FR-017, SC-007 and the configuration contract agree that only the middle third owns volume input and that reserved thirds never fall back to volume? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017, §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK015 Do FR-020, the action contract and `OutputSelection` agree that actions cannot select an output, relocate a visible OSD or create another instance? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020, Actions Contract, Data Model `OutputSelection.locked`]
- [ ] CHK016 Do fallback requirements use the same priority order across the spec, plan, configuration contract and data model? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020, Plan §Rendering and interaction, Data Model `OutputSelection.screenId`]
- [ ] CHK017 Are scale-factor obligations consistent between SC-006, the four-value automated matrix and the rule that physical two-output evidence cannot be replaced by a single-output run? [Consistency, Spec §SC-006, Plan §Verification and delivery]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK018 Does SC-006 define an objective pass condition for every focused-window and empty-workspace trial, including how wrong-output or duplicate appearances are counted? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK019 Does SC-007 quantify center-zone success, early-leave cancellation, reserved-zone non-activation and boundary evidence separately? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK020 Are acceptance criteria defined for routing-state unavailability, stream loss and recovery rather than only for the healthy focus-follows-mouse path? [Gap, Plan §Multi-output routing and edge zones]
- [ ] CHK021 Are configuration-migration and copy/mirror outcomes represented by measurable success criteria, rather than only design-contract prose? [Gap, Spec §Success Criteria; Configuration Contract]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK022 Are primary scenarios complete for a focused window on each monitor and for pointer-based discovery on each monitor regardless of focus? [Coverage, Spec User Story 1, User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK023 Are alternate scenarios complete for empty workspaces, show-only invocation, binding-driven operation and automatic external-audio summoning? [Coverage, Spec §FR-001, §FR-018–020]
- [ ] CHK024 Are lifecycle scenarios complete when focus changes or another audio event arrives during emergence, interaction and retraction? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases, §FR-008, §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK025 Are exception and recovery requirements defined for focused-output loss, selected-output removal, adapter unavailability and no connected output? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases, Plan §Multi-output routing and edge zones]
- [ ] CHK026 Are shared-edge reachability and pointer crossing between adjacent monitors explicitly classified as acceptance gates rather than assumed behavior? [Coverage, Plan §Gate status, Quickstart §Pre-implementation feasibility gate]
- [ ] CHK027 Are requirements for more than two connected outputs explicit, including whether named copy/mirror profiles remain active and how a single OSD is selected? [Gap, Spec §FR-020, Configuration Contract §Per-output trigger profiles]
- [ ] CHK028 Are invalid, self-referential, cyclic, over-limit and disconnected output profiles covered by requirements with per-profile fallback and diagnostics? [Coverage, Configuration Contract §Per-output trigger profiles, Data Model `EdgeTriggerProfile.*`]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK029 Are latency requirements stated for the added routing path without weakening the existing 500 ms presentation target? [Performance, Spec §SC-002, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK030 Are bounded-resource requirements explicit for focus observation, sensor count, reconnection and dormant behavior, including the prohibition on recurring polling and full-screen capture? [Performance, Constitution IV, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK031 Are focus preservation, stable targets, reduced motion and non-colour mute distinction requirements still complete for both left- and right-side placement? [Accessibility, Constitution II, Spec §FR-002, §FR-005–010]
- [ ] CHK032 Are privacy requirements explicit about excluding private compositor configuration, window titles and personal desktop content from diagnostics and evidence? [Privacy, Constitution VI, Quickstart §Prerequisites]
- [ ] CHK033 Are top/bottom pass-through and the narrow sensor’s unavoidable input ownership described precisely enough to assess interference with existing applications? [Interaction Safety, Plan §Input design, Spec §FR-017]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK034 Is focus-follows-mouse documented as a platform prerequisite for the empty-workspace pointer fallback on Niri 26.04, with an explicit return-to-spec outcome if live evidence fails? [Dependency, Plan §Platform routing]
- [ ] CHK035 Are supported Niri, Quickshell and scale baselines distinguished from versions and hardware that remain unverified? [Assumption, Plan §Technical Context, Quickstart §Prerequisites]
- [ ] CHK036 Is the absence of a dependable compositor work-area source documented consistently as a limitation rather than an unsupported capability claim? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions, Research §Logical edge bounds]
- [ ] CHK037 Are temporary scale changes, user authorization and the requirement to leave SC-006 open when the physical matrix is unavailable stated consistently? [Safety, Plan §Verification and delivery, Quickstart §End-to-end and visual checks]

## Ambiguities and Conflicts

- [ ] CHK038 Is the apparent difference between “exactly two displays” in copy/mirror acceptance and named profiles that can exist with more outputs intentionally resolved? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-011, Configuration Contract §Per-output trigger profiles]
- [ ] CHK039 Is the historical “configured display” terminology fully superseded by focused-output routing plus `fallbackOutput`, with no remaining requirement that implies fixed primary placement? [Ambiguity, Spec Clarifications, Configuration Contract §Schema-v1 migration]
- [ ] CHK040 Does the documentation distinguish a copied edge configuration from duplicating the visible OSD everywhere the term “copy” or “duplicate” appears? [Clarity, Spec Clarifications 2026-11-23, Data Model `EdgeTriggerProfile.mirror`]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline and link them to the governing artifact
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
